accueil.titre: Help Batack open its health centre
accueil.intro: The health centre building is there. Before it can welcome its first patients, it still needs a solid roof, electrical wiring and medical equipment. Each donation funds one of these steps, and you then see what it was used for.
accueil.projetsIntro: The village committee decides the order of the work. The amounts shown are examples until the COVIDEBA provides the real figures.

aproposTexte: The COVIDEBA is the development committee of the village of Batack. It leads the village projects: drinking water, schools, health.

ConnectBatack 3 brings together the COVIDEBA, students from the Faculty of Engineering of Mons (UMONS) and the National Advanced School of Engineering of Yaoundé (ENSPY). The first two phases installed a solar microgrid and built the health centre building.
accueil.appelTexte: You can donate without creating an account, once or every month.
accueil.besoinTexte: First step of the works: protect the building before installing electricity and medical equipment.
accueil.parallaxeTexte: From the solar charging station to the health centre, each phase starts from a need expressed by the village of Batack.

dispensaire.titre: Complete and equip the health centre
dispensaire.description: Today, the people of Batack have to travel more than 20 km to reach the nearest health centre. Every consultation, even for everyday care, means making this long journey. The health centre building has already been built in the village, but it cannot welcome patients yet. To open it, the roof must be finished, the electrical wiring installed, and then the laboratory and X-ray equipment bought.

batteries.titre: Solar power for the health centre
batteries.description: In January 2026, Connect Batack 2 equipped the health centre with solar panels and batteries. They power the refrigerator that stores vaccines and the lighting for night-time care. Batteries wear out: this project funds their regular maintenance, then their replacement, so that the health centre does not depend on an unreliable power grid.
batteries.accroche: Ensure the health centre's energy self-sufficiency

ecole.description: Batack has schools, but their classrooms are dark and cramped. The COVIDEBA also has to pay teachers every month. This project funds a teacher's salary, so that primary school children have classes all year round.
ecole.accroche: Guarantee basic education for primary school children

eau.description: The COVIDEBA has already built a first drinking water network. This project extends it to the areas that are still far from it, so that more families have drinking water near their homes. The route and the cost will be set with the COVIDEBA.
eau.accroche: Make drinking water accessible to all

histoire.intro: Since 2024, engineering students from Mons and Yaoundé have been working with the Batack village committee. Each phase starts from a need expressed by the village, and the next one checks that the previous one still works.

etapes.texte: The Faculty of Engineering of Mons starts working with four Cameroonian universities, in Yaoundé and Douala, on engineering education. These exchanges bring to light the needs of villages far from cities, including Batack.

The first student microprojects are launched with the support of ARES. They bring together the Faculty of Engineering of Mons (UMONS), the National Advanced School of Engineering of Yaoundé (ENSPY) and the COVIDEBA.
First achievement: a public solar charging station for phones and lamps, in a village without a reliable power grid. A year later, the next team checked that it was still working.

etapes.titre: Connect Batack 2: power for the health centre
etapes.texte: From 24 to 30 January 2026, the team installs a stand-alone solar system at the health centre: a refrigerator to store vaccines and lighting for night-time care. The work is done with local technicians and the COVIDEBA, so that the village can maintain the installation.

The health centre is built but not yet in service, and the nearest hospital is 20 km away. This last phase with UMONS creates this donation site, prepares the technical file for the health centre and looks for lasting funding, in Europe and in Cameroon. A mission to the village is planned for January 2027.

histoire.aujourdhuiIntro: Batack is a village in Bamileke country, in the highlands of West Cameroon. Its inhabitants, who call themselves the "little people of Batack", have already carried out several projects.

lieux.texte: A primary school with a computer room, then a nursery school built with the support of Italian cooperation.

transparence.intro: You should be able to check what happens to every euro. This page brings together the amounts received, the expenses and the way the committee decides.
transparence.miseAJour: Example figures. They will be calculated automatically from the register.
transparence.repartitionIntro: Your donation is split into three parts. The percentages below are examples: the real figures will be published after the first year.
transparence.methode: Method: payment fees are those charged by Stripe and the bank. Other costs include website hosting and money transfers to Cameroon. There is no single definition of "costs": we will always state what each part contains.
transparence.registreIntro: Every significant expense is published with its invoice or a photo, and with the minutes of the COVIDEBA meeting that approved it. An entry is never deleted: a mistake is corrected by a new entry, which is also visible.
transparence.registreVide: The first expenses will appear here once the management area is up and running.
decisionPoints: Priorities are set by the COVIDEBA, together with the village health workers.
A calculation tool suggests the order of expenses while respecting the order of the works: the roof comes before the medical equipment.
A safety reserve, set by the chieftaincy, always stays in the fund.
The final decision belongs to the committee: the tool suggests, the committee decides.
transparence.rapportsTexte: An annual report, with the accounts, will be published here as a PDF.

apropos.intro: This site is published by the village committee. Engineering students from Belgium and Cameroon designed it together with the committee.
covidebaTexte: The Batack Village Development Committee (COVIDEBA) brings together residents and members of the Batack community. It leads the village projects and decides how funds are used.
It is chaired by Dr Anatole Chengoué.
apropos.equipesTexte: Connect Batack 3 brings together students from the Faculty of Engineering of the University of Mons (computer science and management, mechanics, energy) and from the National Advanced School of Engineering of Yaoundé (industrial engineering, mechanics, computer science).

apropos.charteIntro: The Mons and Yaoundé teams work according to five principles.
charte: Mutual respect: each member is a full partner, and cultural differences are an asset.
Shared decisions: important decisions are discussed and approved by both teams.
Recognising everyone's work and every success, even small ones.
Availability and transparency: everyone gives advance notice of absence, delay or difficulty.
